rationale: Two major patch findings: (1) Avatar iconUrl prop uses `currentChat?.assistantData[0]?.iconUrl` without optional chaining on [0], inconsistent with the defensive ?. already applied to assistantData.length in the same condition — latent crash risk if assistantData is ever absent. (2) A group chat with exactly 1 assistant satisfies both the isGroup section condition (isGroup=true && length>0) and the new single-assistant section condition (assistantDisplayName truthy as joined name + length<=1), producing duplicate Avatar rendering. Acceptance: 5/6 criteria pass; screenshot verification is manual QA scope. Standards: commit format valid, TypeScript and ESLint clean.
follow_ups: Add `!currentChat?.isGroup` guard to the single-assistant block condition in ChatHeader.tsx

findings.problem: Avatar iconUrl prop uses `currentChat?.assistantData[0]?.iconUrl` without optional chaining on [0], inconsistent with the defensive `?.` already applied to `assistantData.length` in the same outer condition.
findings.impact: If assistantData is absent or null at runtime, `undefined[0]` throws a TypeError that crashes the ChatHeader component.

findings.problem: A group chat with exactly 1 assistant satisfies both the isGroup block condition (`isGroup=true && assistantData.length===1 > 0`) and the new single-assistant block condition (`assistantDisplayName` truthy as joined name + `length <= 1`). Both blocks render simultaneously, producing two Avatar components for the same assistant.
findings.impact: Group chats that have or transition to exactly 1 member show a duplicate avatar in the header. The second Avatar's click handler also fires `handleAvatarClick`, creating confusing interaction.
findings.recommendation: Add `!currentChat?.isGroup` to the single-assistant block condition: `{assistantDisplayName && !currentChat?.isGroup && (currentChat?.assistantData?.length ?? 0) <= 1 && ...}`.
